summary: Set 131 Session 2 of 3, 'The number that is not a price'. ai_router/copilot-catalog.lock carried a per-model number called premium_request_weight, populated from the premium-request count the Copilot CLI reported for the ONE short probe call that confirmed the model. The name asserted a rate; the value was a single call's consumption. Measured against the seat store on 2026-08-14 it disagrees with the authoritative request_multiplier for the entire OpenAI family (gpt-5.5 probes 0 and bills 7.5, the second-highest multiplier on the seat) while the Anthropic and Google entries happen to agree, which is exactly what made it look trustworthy. The defect was latent because nothing read it for selection; Session 1's widening of delegation is what would have created that reader. DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION, journaled in decisions.jsonl: the reference kept the name and wrapped it in a NOT-A-PRICE comment, while spec.md step 2 says to rename it and the spec's own irony-budget note says 'the field's NAME was the defect'. Renamed to probe_premium_requests, bumped the lockfile schema v1 -> v2 behind LOCKFILE_SCHEMA_VERSION, and kept a legacy read (_LEGACY_PROBE_PREMIUM_KEY) so no existing seat lockfile loses a real measurement - confirmed against the live 18-model seat file, which still loads with values intact (gpt-5.5 -> 0, claude-haiku-4.5 -> None). Pinned to the declaration: the measured OpenAI-family disagreement, the fail-closed rule that None means UNKNOWN and never free (L-112-1), and the credit-axis decoupling - at matched context claude-opus-5 (multiplier 15.0) and gpt-5.5 (7.5) cost the same per inference, so correcting the numbers would still not make the field usable for selection, which is the conclusion a reader would otherwise reach. A genuine 0 was deliberately NOT coerced to None: 0 is a true measurement of what that probe consumed, and mapping it to None would make the lockfile assert 'never probed' about a model that was probed. The field is disarmed by interpretation instead - an absolute prohibition on naming it outside copilot_catalog.py, which is strictly stronger than fixing the zero case. Both verifiers raised that reading and both rated it Nit and defensible. FALSIFICATION BY PLANTING, NOT BY READING (L-112-1): the new ai_router/tests/test_catalog_weight_not_a_price.py ships 8 falsifiers, and every one was proven by applying the defect to the real tree, running the named test, and restoring the file - 10 plants, 10 fired. They include the two halves L-112-1 asks for: the prohibition fires on a new reader (both spellings, and on a nested file that borrows the permitted basename), and the legitimate look-alike does NOT fire (cli_transport.py and copilot_preflight.py carry a real premium_requests transport-metadata key; a plant that widened the scan to a naive substring was caught by that test). The scan also asserts its own corpus is non-empty and contains named members, so it cannot pass having examined nothing. TEST COMPOSITION (project-guidance requires this be stated, not presented as one clean run): pytest 4490 passed / 9 skipped in one invocation (758s), which is exactly +8 over Session 1's 4482 and accounts for the whole new module - then re-run end to end a second time (1005s, identical 4490/9) because the A4 round below wrote artifacts under docs/session-sets/, which pytest declares as a covered surface, staling the first run; no code changed between the two; mocha 1455 passing / 2 pending in one invocation (35s); playwright 30 passed in the declared invocation (7.9m) with vsix-first-run-walkthrough failing on a 300s load-induced timeout, then that one spec re-run in isolation and passing in 56.6s - the identical spec, identical assertions, and the identical failure Session 1 hit for the identical reason. Every test in all three suites executed and passed; the route is journaled in decisions.jsonl. Cross-provider verification returned VERIFIED on round 1 with 0 blocking findings (2-way fan-out, both calls gpt-5.5, anthropic excluded as the orchestrator's effective provider). Five Nits were recorded and adjudicated: (1)+(2) both verifiers noted the un-coerced zero, accepted as by-design above; (3) the prohibition allowlist matched on basename, so a nested file could borrow the name - FIXED, the allowlist is now path-relative and a new plant proves the hole is closed; (4) the Set 078 design doc still spells the old name and the module docstring pointed at it as authoritative - FIXED, the pointer now says that document is a v1-era artifact and ModelEntry wins (L-064-8); (5) dumps(loads(v1_lock)) emits v2 field names under a v1 schema label - DEFERRED RESIDUAL, no load-then-write migration path exists in this repo (main() always writes a freshly discovered catalog, which stamps v2), and the reasoning plus the obligation on any future migration is now written into the LOCKFILE_SCHEMA_VERSION comment. The three post-round fixes were comment-only and test-only, changing no shipped behaviour, so no additional verification round was opened on my own judgment; the plants were re-run afterwards and all 10 still fire. The close gate disagreed with that judgment on the letter - post_round_delta classified the delta as shipped-code because two changed paths sit outside a declared test surface - so round 2 was run as the A4 obligation names: a delta-scoped remediation-review against the round-1 baseline tree, verifier gpt-5.5 with anthropic excluded, carrying a conventions block that named all three edits and nothing else. It returned VERIFIED with 0 findings. Running it here rather than meeting it inside close_session is the point: the same round costs the same money either way, but only this way could its findings have been iterated on.

The measured cost lever is transcript rotation at ~7-8x, not model substitution at ~1.7-2x matched context, so hold the orchestrator constant and manage cost through compaction discipline instead.
